status_reason: The recommendation is a theoretical proposal attributed to Mead and summarized by Monroe, with no intervention study or synthesis testing whether this balance produces continual adaptation or learning.

status_reason: Research supports related claims about selection bias, expectation effects, developmental resources, and the domain-specific nature of talent, but does not directly test this combined recommendation or establish that perceived giftedness mainly operates through resource access.

works.title: Methods and Results in the Study of Anxiety and Language Learning: A Review of the Literature

recommendation: Begin post-screening film discussion with students’ spontaneous impressions and emotions, and only then move to contextual, critical, and narratological analysis.

works.title: Strategies for Teaching Students to Think Critically: A Meta-Analysis

recommendation: Teach data storytelling through a Forage–Remix–DIY progression in which learners analyze existing stories, reconstruct and alter an exemplary story, then author and publicly defend an original open-data story.
status_reason: No independent research appears to test this exact three-stage sequence, but reviews and studies support related claims about data-literacy instruction, generative production, active engagement, and feedback.

works.title: Strategies and Best Practices for Data Literacy Education: Knowledge Synthesis Report
works.bears_on: Synthesizes approaches to developing data-literacy knowledge and practices, but does not test the Forage–Remix–DIY sequence.

works.title: Eight Ways to Promote Generative Learning

works.title: Classroom dialogue: A systematic review across four decades of research

status_reason: Research supports the broader value of form-focused, meaningful, and interaction-based instruction, but has not directly tested this entire practice spectrum or the recommendation to introduce each type as early as possible.

recommendation: Ground EDI initiatives in an explicit commitment to disrupting systems of power and oppression rather than inclusion alone.

works.title: A Meta-Analytical Integration of Over 40 Years of Research on Diversity Training Evaluation

recommendation: Teach self-regulation processes such as planning and monitoring together with scientific-reasoning skills such as hypothesis generation and evidence evaluation rather than in separate modules.

works.title: Developing Literacy in English Language Learners: Report of the National Literacy Panel on Language-Minority Children and Youth
works.bears_on: Synthesizes evidence that oral language, vocabulary, and phonological skills contribute to second-language literacy development without testing an oral-first instructional sequence.

works.title: Reading Comprehension and Its Underlying Components in Second-Language Learners: A Meta-Analysis
works.bears_on: Tests associations between second-language reading comprehension and oral-language-related components, rather than the recommended order of instruction.

crossref.title: Reading comprehension and its underlying components in second-language learners: A meta-analysis of studies comparing first- and second-language learners.

works.title: L2 Reading Comprehension and Its Correlates: A Meta-Analysis
works.bears_on: Finds that vocabulary, grammar, and other language abilities are related to L2 reading comprehension, providing indirect support for the importance of oral-language foundations.

crossref.title: L2 Reading Comprehension and Its Correlates: A Meta‐Analysis

recommendation: Allow young learners to engage in practice play under relaxed conditions so that motor skills can consolidate into modular, efficient, and transferable forms.
status_reason: Research supports related claims about play-based practice, implicit motor learning, and the vulnerability of consciously controlled skills under pressure, but does not directly test this complete recommendation or its proposed modularization mechanism.

works.title: Practice and play in the development of sport expertise
works.bears_on: Reviews evidence that playful, varied practice contributes to skill development, though not specifically through modularization in relaxed conditions.

crossref.title: Practice and Play in the Development of Sport Expertise

works.title: Optimizing performance through intrinsic motivation and attention for learning: The OPTIMAL theory of motor learning
works.bears_on: Synthesizes evidence that autonomy, positive expectancies, and less constrained attention can support motor learning and performance.

works.title: Knowledge, knerves and know-how: The role of implicit learning in the acquisition of skilled motor performance
works.bears_on: Shows that implicitly acquired motor skills can be relatively robust under pressure, supporting a nearby claim about reducing reliance on consciously controlled procedures.

works.title: On the fragility of skilled performance: What governs choking under pressure?
works.bears_on: Demonstrates that pressure can disrupt skilled performance when attention is directed toward normally automated or procedural actions.

crossref.title: On the Fragility of Skilled Performance: What Governs Choking under Pressure?

recommendation: Teachers cannot directly teach mental representations or skills, but should provide learning experiences and use instructional research to choose among them.
status_reason: Meta-analyses show that instruction can produce measurable L2 learning, but they do not directly test the stronger claim that instruction cannot intervene in learners’ underlying representations or skills.

works.title: Effectiveness of L2 Instruction: A Research Synthesis and Quantitative Meta-analysis
works.bears_on: Tests whether instructional treatments produce measurable second-language learning.

crossref.title: Effectiveness of L2 Instruction: A Research Synthesis and Quantitative Meta‐analysis

works.title: Interactions Between Type of Instruction and Type of Language Feature: A Meta-Analysis
works.bears_on: Tests whether different instructional approaches affect acquisition of particular L2 features.

crossref.title: Interactions Between Type of Instruction and Type of Language Feature: A Meta‐Analysis

recommendation: History instruction should treat imagination as a central, legitimate component of evidence-constrained historical knowledge construction rather than as mere fiction-making.
status_reason: Research has examined related practices such as historical empathy, perspective-taking, and evidence-based imaginative reconstruction, but has not directly tested this broad design principle as a whole.

works.title: An updated theoretical and practical model for promoting historical empathy
works.bears_on: Synthesizes research and theory on using contextualized perspective-taking and evidence to develop historical empathy.

works.title: Displaying historical empathy: What impact can a writing assignment have?
works.bears_on: Tests whether an evidence-informed historical writing task can promote students’ expression of historical empathy.

crossref.title: Displaying Historical Empathy: What Impact Can a Writing Assignment Have?

recommendation: Build trusting, emotionally safe teacher-student and student-student relationships as a sustained foundation for equitable scientific argumentation and public revision of ideas.
status_reason: Research supports the broader links between positive relationships, school safety, engagement, and participation, but has not directly and causally tested relationship-building as a prerequisite for scientific argumentation.

works.title: The influence of affective teacher–student relationships on students’ school engagement and achievement: A meta-analytic approach
works.bears_on: Positive teacher-student relationships are associated with greater student engagement, a prerequisite for sustained classroom discourse.

crossref.title: The Influence of Affective Teacher–Student Relationships on Students’ School Engagement and Achievement

works.title: Learner-centered teacher-student relationships are effective: A meta-analysis
works.bears_on: Supportive, learner-centered relationships are associated with beneficial student engagement and learning outcomes.

crossref.title: Learner-Centered Teacher-Student Relationships Are Effective: A                Meta-Analysis

works.title: A Review of School Climate Research
works.bears_on: Safety, supportive relationships, and student connectedness are central dimensions of a positive school climate.

works.title: Framing the Problem of Productive Disciplinary Engagement
works.bears_on: Classroom norms, accountability, and participation structures help make sustained disciplinary discourse possible, though relationships are not isolated as a causal prerequisite.

recommendation: Use stochastic approximation for sequential parameter estimation when observations are noisy and each observation is costly.
status_reason: Foundational and later mathematical research supports convergence for noisy sequential estimation under suitable step-size conditions, but there is little direct empirical testing of this recommendation in costly adaptive learner-assessment settings.

works.title: A Stochastic Approximation Method
works.bears_on: Introduces the Robbins–Monro procedure and proves convergence for sequential estimation from noisy observations.

crossref.title: A Stochastic Approximation Method

works.title: Stochastic Estimation of the Maximum of a Regression Function
works.bears_on: Extends stochastic approximation to sequential optimization when observations are noisy.

crossref.title: Stochastic Estimation of the Maximum of a Regression Function

works.title: Multidimensional Stochastic Approximation Methods
works.bears_on: Establishes convergence results for multidimensional sequential stochastic approximation.

crossref.title: Multidimensional Stochastic Approximation Methods

works.title: Stochastic Approximation and Recursive Algorithms and Applications
works.bears_on: Synthesizes convergence theory and applications for recursive estimation under noisy observations.

crossref.title: Stochastic Approximation and Recursive Algorithms and Applications

recommendation: Build instruction responsively from students' expressed interests as they arise rather than relying primarily on goals and activities predetermined by teachers or curriculum writers.
status_reason: Research supports nearby components such as learner choice, personalization, and situational interest, but there is little direct comparative evidence testing fully emergent curriculum against predetermined curricula.

works.title: The effects of choice on intrinsic motivation and related outcomes: A meta-analysis of research findings
works.bears_on: Tests whether giving learners meaningful choices improves motivation and related learning outcomes.

works.title: Intrinsic motivation and the process of learning: Beneficial effects of contextualization, personalization, and choice
works.bears_on: Tests whether personalization and learner choice increase interest and learning.

crossref.title: Intrinsic motivation and the process of learning: Beneficial effects of contextualization, personalization, and choice.

works.title: Effect of choice on cognitive and affective engagement
works.bears_on: Tests whether student choice increases engagement during classroom learning.

crossref.title: Effect of Choice on Cognitive and Affective Engagement

works.title: The Four-Phase Model of Interest Development
works.bears_on: Explains how situational interest can be triggered and developed into more enduring individual interest.

crossref.title: The Four-Phase Model of Interest Development

recommendation: Use a five-step lesson sequence that reviews prior learning, prepares learners with an overview, presents new material, explicitly relates it to prior learning, and supports application.
status_reason: Research supports several component claims about activating prior knowledge, advance organizers, and retrieval practice, but does not establish that Herbart's complete five-step sequence is superior as a unified lesson design.

works.title: A Meta-Analysis of the Effects of Advance Organizers on Learning and Retention
works.bears_on: tests the value of providing an orienting framework before new material

crossref.title: A Meta-analysis of the Effects of Advance Organizers on Learning and                Retention

works.title: The Relation Between Assessment of Prior Knowledge and Learning Outcomes: A Meta-Analysis
works.bears_on: supports the importance of learners' prior knowledge for subsequent learning outcomes

works.title: Retrieval Practice Produces More Learning than Elaborative Studying with Concept Mapping
works.bears_on: supports retrieval-based review as a potentially effective component of the sequence

crossref.title: Retrieval Practice Produces More Learning than Elaborative Studying with Concept Mapping

recommendation: Provide short-form support, information, or practice at the moment it is needed for performance.
status_reason: Empirical studies of Just-in-Time Teaching and web-based pre-performance preparation support the broader idea of timely learning support, but do not directly test the full canonical pattern across contexts.

works.title: Transforming common-sense beliefs into Newtonian thinking through Just-in-Time Teaching
works.bears_on: Tests whether instruction delivered through a Just-in-Time Teaching sequence improves students’ conceptual understanding.

crossref.title: Transforming common-sense beliefs into Newtonian thinking through Just-In-Time Teaching

works.title: Web-based warm up exercises in university physics
works.bears_on: Tests web-based, immediately preceding preparation activities associated with Just-in-Time Teaching.

recommendation: For learner models intended to transfer to unseen student populations, avoid fixed or random student intercepts and instead model student differences with features computed from each student's current practice sequence.
status_reason: Studies compare sequence-based learner models with individualized models and discuss cold-start generalization, but few directly test whether omitting student intercepts improves transfer to entirely new student populations.

works.title: Bayesian Knowledge Tracing, Logistic Models, and Beyond: An Overview of Learner Modeling Techniques
works.bears_on: reviews the trade-off between student-specific parameters and dynamic, sequence-based features in learner models

crossref.title: Bayesian knowledge tracing, logistic models, and beyond: an overview of learner modeling techniques

works.title: Individualized Bayesian Knowledge Tracing Models
works.bears_on: tests whether student-specific parameters improve prediction, providing evidence about the cost and benefit of intercept-like individualization

works.title: Modeling Individualization in a Bayesian Networks Implementation of Knowledge Tracing
works.bears_on: evaluates models that represent individual student differences rather than relying only on shared learner parameters

crossref.title: Modeling Individualization in a Bayesian Networks Implementation of Knowledge Tracing

works.title: Deep Knowledge Tracing
works.bears_on: shows that a sequence-based model can capture learner variation without explicitly estimating a separate student intercept

recommendation: Developers of locus-of-control instruments should balance the situations and external sources of control represented in items because item composition affects obtained scores.
status_reason: Several independent empirical studies have shown that locus-of-control instruments contain separable situation- and source-related dimensions, indicating that item composition can change the construct being measured and relations among scores.

works.title: Four components of the Rotter Internal-External Scale: Belief in a difficult world, a just world, a predictable world, and a politically responsive world

crossref.title: Four components of the Rotter Internal-External scale: Belief in a difficult world, a just world, a predictable world, and a politically responsive world.

works.title: Dimensions of internal versus external control

crossref.title: Dimensions of internal versus external control.

works.title: Multidimensional locus of control in psychiatric patients
works.bears_on: Separating internal control, chance, and powerful others shows that the measured locus-of-control score depends on which external sources the instrument samples.

crossref.title: Multidimensional locus of control in psychiatric patients.

recommendation: Bind task-based language teaching and language testing so that task-based assessment harnesses assessment washback to shape instruction and learning.
status_reason: Research has examined whether language tests, including IELTS, influence teaching and learning, but it provides limited direct evidence that deliberately binding task-based teaching and assessment produces beneficial washback.

works.title: Washback in Language Testing: Research Contexts and Methods
works.bears_on: Synthesizes research showing that language assessments can influence classroom teaching and learning, while emphasizing that washback is variable rather than automatic.

crossref.title: Washback in Language Testing

works.title: Does Washback Exist?
works.bears_on: Establishes the central empirical question and argues that test effects on teaching and learning require investigation rather than being assumed.

crossref.title: Does Washback Exist?

works.title: IELTS Washback in Context: Preparation for Academic Writing in Higher Education
works.bears_on: Investigates how IELTS preparation shapes instructional practices and learner activity, providing evidence for test-related washback but not specifically for task-based assessment-teaching alignment.

recommendation: Treat datafication as a rhetorical and situated practice rather than objective representation, and practice metadistrust by critically examining data-based arguments before accepting them.
status_reason: Research has tested related claims about overtrust, distrust, transparency, and calibrated reliance on algorithmic or quantitative advice, but not the specific practice of metadistrust toward datafication as rhetoric.

works.title: Trust in Automation: Designing for Appropriate Reliance
works.bears_on: Explains why people need calibrated rather than indiscriminate trust or distrust in automated and data-based systems.

works.title: Algorithm Aversion: People Erroneously Avoid Algorithms After Seeing Them Err
works.bears_on: Shows that people can respond to algorithmic advice with maladaptive distrust rather than appropriately calibrated evaluation.

crossref.title: Algorithm Aversion: People Erroneously Avoid Algorithms after Seeing Them Err

works.title: Algorithm Appreciation: People Prefer Algorithmic to Human Judgment
works.bears_on: Shows the complementary risk of excessive deference to algorithmic judgments and data-based authority.

crossref.title: Algorithm appreciation: People prefer algorithmic to human judgment

works.title: Motivated Numeracy and Enlightened Self-Government
works.bears_on: Shows that quantitative reasoning can be shaped by prior commitments, supporting scrutiny of apparently objective data-based arguments.

crossref.title: Motivated numeracy and enlightened self-government

recommendation: High-stakes examinations should generally target a decision-consistency estimate of at least 0.85, while interpreting lower estimates in light of cut-score location, score reliability, and population heterogeneity.
status_reason: Methodological and empirical research tests how decision consistency varies with cut-score location, score distributions, reliability, and classification procedures, but does not establish 0.85 as a universally validated threshold for all high-stakes examinations.

works.title: Estimating the Consistency and Accuracy of Classifications Based on Test Scores
works.bears_on: Shows how classification consistency and accuracy depend on score reliability, the cut score, and the score distribution.

crossref.title: Estimating the Consistency and Accuracy of Classifications Based on Test Scores

works.title: A Comparison of Two Procedures for Assessing the Consistency and Accuracy of Performance Standards
works.bears_on: Compares procedures for estimating classification consistency and accuracy and demonstrates that estimates can differ with performance-standard and distributional conditions.

recommendation: Teach learners to communicate both congruently and incongruently and to judge which mode is appropriate in a given social and cultural context.
status_reason: Research supports teaching context-sensitive social competence and adapting expressive behavior to situational demands, but no identified study directly tests instruction in deliberately using both congruent and incongruent communication.

works.title: Effects of training social competence in children: A meta-analysis of recent evaluation studies

crossref.title: Effects of training social competence in children: A meta-analysis of recent evaluation studies

crossref.title: The Impact of Enhancing Students’ Social and Emotional Learning: A Meta-Analysis of School-Based Universal Interventions

works.title: Self-Monitoring of Expressive Behavior

crossref.title: Self-monitoring of expressive behavior.

works.title: Mapping expressive differences around the world: The relationship between emotional display rules and individualism versus collectivism
works.bears_on: demonstrates that culturally variable display rules make the appropriateness of expressive congruence context-dependent

crossref.title: Mapping Expressive Differences Around the World

recommendation: For extensive reading, choose graded readers rather than authentic texts or children's books, and make reading enjoyable, easy, and frequent.
status_reason: Meta-analyses and empirical studies support the broader benefits of extensive reading and its association with positive reading attitudes, but they do not directly establish that graded readers outperform authentic or children's texts or isolate the effects of being fun, easy, and frequent.

works.title: A Meta-Analysis of Extensive Reading Research

works.title: The effectiveness of extensive reading on reading proficiency in a foreign language: A meta-analysis

works.title: Effects of extensive reading on reading attitudes in a foreign language

crossref.title: Effects of extensive reading on reading attitudes in a foreign language

works.bears_on: compares an extensive-reading program with more conventional foreign-language instruction

crossref.title: Extensive reading in English as a foreign language

recommendation: Youth environmental learning programs should involve a local natural-resource professional to provide locally relevant scientific expertise, technical support, and career connections.
status_reason: Research supports benefits of experiential, community-based environmental education and authentic community partnerships, but does not directly test whether recruiting a local natural-resource professional produces the claimed learning outcomes.

works.title: Environmental education outcomes for conservation: A systematic review
works.bears_on: reviews evidence that environmental education can improve conservation-related knowledge, attitudes, and behaviors

crossref.title: Environmental education outcomes for conservation: A systematic review

works.title: Environmental education and K-12 student outcomes: A review and analysis of research

crossref.title: Environmental education and K-12 student outcomes: A review and analysis of research

works.title: Closing the Achievement Gap: Using the Environment as an Integrating Context for Learning
works.bears_on: synthesizes evidence and examples of community-connected environmental learning involving outside expertise

crossref.title: Closing the Achievement Gap

recommendation: Give learners control over the flow of information while providing contextual explanations, glossaries, feedback, and other supports on demand.
status_reason: Research has examined learner-controlled pacing and navigation, but evidence for the broader combination of learner control with on-demand contextual supports is indirect and mixed.

works.bears_on: finds little overall benefit for learner control, with some advantage for learner pacing on complex material

crossref.title: Learner-Control Effects: A Review of Reviews and a Meta-Analysis

crossref.title: When learning is just a click away: Does simple user interaction foster deeper understanding of multimedia messages?

recommendation: Educators should interpret children’s overgeneralized forms such as “goed” and “taked” as evidence of developing rule knowledge and progress rather than as errors or signs of weakness.

works.title: Overregularization in Language Acquisition

crossref.title: Overregularization in Language Acquisition

crossref.title: The Child's Learning of English Morphology

recommendation: Make learning pleasurable and engaging because anticipating pleasure releases dopamine that supports attention, memory, and the processing of new information.
status_reason: Research shows that reward anticipation and curiosity can engage dopaminergic systems and improve subsequent memory, but it has not directly tested whether making ordinary classroom learning pleasurable and engaging produces the broad educational benefits claimed.

works.title: Dopamine and adaptive memory
works.bears_on: Reviews how dopamine and reward-related prediction can influence learning and memory.

crossref.title: Dopamine and adaptive memory

works.title: Reward-motivated learning: mesolimbic activation precedes memory formation

crossref.title: Reward-Motivated Learning: Mesolimbic Activation Precedes Memory Formation

recommendation: Instructional products should provide learners with relevant practice and knowledge of results, omit irrelevancies, and make the material interesting.

works.title: The Seductive Details Effect: A Meta-Analysis
works.bears_on: tests whether including interesting but irrelevant material harms learning

recommendation: Provide young readers with syntactically appropriate texts written by peers rather than basal readers.
status_reason: Research supports the broader claims that young readers use syntactic and contextual information and that features of beginning-reading texts affect accessibility, but it does not directly establish that peer-authored texts outperform basal readers.

works.title: The Influence of Decodability in Early Reading Text on Reading Achievement: A Review of the Research

crossref.title: Text Decodability and the First-grade Reader

works.title: The Role of Word, Sentence, and Discourse Context in the Reading of Children and Adults

recommendation: Coaches should conduct and analyze assessments collaboratively with teachers rather than serving as the sole assessment administrator.
status_reason: Research supports collaborative data use and the development of teachers’ assessment and data-literacy skills, but does not directly test this specific coach-and-teacher assessment arrangement.

works.title: Interventions Promoting Educators’ Use of Data: Research Insights and Gaps

crossref.title: Interventions Promoting Educators’ Use of Data: Research Insights and Gaps

crossref.title: Strategies to Promote Data Use for Instructional Improvement: Actions, Outcomes, and Lessons fromThree Urban Districts

crossref.title: New Conceptualizations of Practice: Common Principles in Three Paradigms Suggest New Concepts for Training

crossref.title: Distribution of Practice in Motor Skill Acquisition: Different Effects for Discrete and Continuous Tasks

recommendation: Teach style as attention to how language choices shape meaning and audience effects, rather than as a set of prescriptive rules.
status_reason: Research has tested contextualized, meaning-focused grammar instruction and contrasted it with traditional rule teaching, but has not directly tested this critical-pedagogical account of style instruction.

works.title: Re-thinking grammar: the impact of embedded grammar teaching on students' writing and students' metalinguistic understanding

recommendation: Teachers should support students with ADHD through structure, predictability, and explicit self-monitoring instruction, rather than relying on medication decisions outside their control.
status_reason: Behavioral classroom-management and self-regulation interventions support nearby components of this recommendation, but research has not directly tested the entire combined claim about structure, predictability, self-monitoring, and classroom aggravation.

works.title: School-Based Interventions for Students with Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder: Current Status and Future Directions
works.bears_on: summarizes school-based interventions targeting classroom behavior and academic functioning

recommendation: Teach new information for which learners have some prior related knowledge, because familiarity stimulates elaborative processing that supports later retrieval.
status_reason: Research supports the broader claim that prior knowledge affects learning and delayed recall, but has not consistently tested the full instructional recommendation and its proposed elaborative-processing mechanism.

works.title: The relation between assessment of prior knowledge and learning outcome: A meta-analysis

recommendation: When learners cannot yet identify a lesson’s essential elements and organization, add cues such as headings, highlighting, arrows, linked colors, or spoken emphasis to guide attention to them and their connections.

recommendation: For learners preparing for risky, costly, rare, or invisible performances, repeated guided practice in a simulation that preserves task-relevant decisions and cues, followed by feedback or debriefing, should improve performance on the represented task more than no practice or non-simulated instruction, while greater immersion alone should not add learning.
status_reason: Meta-analyses support benefits of simulation and deliberate-practice formats over no intervention or conventional instruction, but the combined effects of guidance, repeated runs, debriefing, task fidelity, and immersion have not been tested together or cleanly isolated.

status_reason: Research supports several ingredients—specific goals, task-level feedback, and reflection—but no identified study directly tests the complete skills-sprint cycle against open-ended projects or isolated exercises.

recommendation: For learners able to contribute to a multi-week group task, make group success depend on every member’s individually assessed learning through shared goals, team recognition, and, where useful, distinct roles or resources, so that members help and hold one another accountable and individual achievement increases.
status_reason: Published reviews and meta-analyses support the reward-plus-individual-accountability component, but the full combination of goal, resource, role, and reward interdependence has not been tested as a whole.

recommendation: In online or blended group courses, deliberately create opportunities for learners to be seen and heard as people—through course-related introductions, visible instructors, stable small groups, structured peer replies, supportive norms, and some live contact—to increase open participation and persistence.
status_reason: Meta-analytic and empirical research supports associations between social presence, instructor connectedness, belonging, engagement, and satisfaction, and tests some individual design moves, but no study directly tests this combined design recommendation and its effects on participation or persistence.

crossref.title: Spaced Repetition Promotes Efficient and Effective Learning

recommendation: A standardized test should support selection or placement decisions equally well across groups only when its items are free of group-related bias, its scores predict later outcomes equally accurately, and testing conditions do not differentially depress performance.
status_reason: Independent research has examined differential item functioning, differential prediction, and group differences under anxiety or stereotype-threatening conditions, but no study or synthesis tests the full three-condition decision-fairness relationship together.
